text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait's response to the issue of reviving ties with Jordan has not matched Amman's initiatives, Prime Minister Kabariti tells ad-Dustour.
- King Hussein meets representative of President Arafat, speaks to Arafat by phone.
- Crown Prince Hassan speaks to meeting of U.N. Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees.
- Information Minister Muasher, in Israel, says Israeli- Jordanian relations are going through a difficult patch. Calls for halt to settlements and complete return of Golan Heights to Syria.
- Oil companies in Baghdad relay messages back to Washington. Promises of opening up in Baghdad's internal and external politics in return for lifting of sanctions within two years.
- Israeli Foreign Minister Levy assures Jordan that his country is committed to implementing Oslo deal on Palestinian self-rule.
- Transport agents demand cuts in Aqaba port tolls.
- Jordan cautions against cuts in refugee services.
- Parliamentary delegates complain of delays in government responses to their queries.
